metaDesc: The AXEM-SX Control Hub, the Desktop Snapshot Manager, Soft Depot, the Boh-IO console sidecar, and the full technical architecture of the Digital Workshop — all local, all sovereign.
heroSub: Every tool in AXEM-SX is crafted with intention — from the first boot to your deepest workflow.
hubHeadline: Your workstation, governed from your workstation.
hubSub: Tiered local administration. Nothing phones home. Nothing routes through someone else's cloud.
hubLead: Most distributions dropped YaST in favor of "modern" web tools that depend on vendor clouds. AXEM-SX kept YaST AND added Cockpit AND wrote a native Qt6 daily-driver — and pinned every layer to your machine. Three tiers, one roof. Pick the right tool for the moment.
hubTier1Desc: Modular Qt6 app. KDE / LXQt / GNOME-aware at runtime. Bridges system settings, desktop modules, and the Desktop Snapshot system into one calm window.
hubTier2Desc: Three decades of openSUSE administration discipline. Kept available — not retired — for the moments that demand it.
hubTier3Desc: Web admin at localhost:9090. Logs, services, storage, networking — readable from any browser on the machine.
hubBreadthLabel: The surface — a sample, not exhaustive
hubBreadthList: Storage · Networking · Users · Services · Logs · Snapshots · Firewall · NTP · DNS · Btrfs · KVM/libvirt · Containers · kdump · …
hubScreenshotCaption: AXEM-SX Control Hub — and this is just the surface.
hubFootnote: Cockpit can be exposed beyond localhost if you choose. AXEM-SX does not enable that for you. Sovereignty is a default, not a cage.
snapHeadline: Roam the Linux desktop spectrum. Without leaving home.
snapSub: Switch desktops. Keep your AXEM-SX. Same packages, same identity, same data — different visual register.
snapLead: Most users pick a desktop once and live with it for years. AXEM-SX gives you a curated way to taste the spectrum without abandoning the workstation you've built. The Desktop Snapshot Manager — a module of axem-control-hub — handles the orchestration.
snap1Desc: The full Pro environment. Wayland session by default.
snap2Desc: Lighter Qt-based desktop. Same Hub, same identity.
snap3Desc: Detected when present. Pure Shell UX honored — no AXEM panel injection.
snapSessionNote: Session-aware: kanshi on Wayland · lxqt-config-monitor on X11 · graceful degradation when backends are absent.
snapHonest: v0.9 module. Surface and flavor coverage will broaden in upcoming releases. Today's verified switch path runs along KDE / LXQt / GNOME runtime detection.
depotDesc: A curated software hub for AXEM-SX. Browse, install, and manage applications with precision — no flood of duplicates, no telemetry, no buried dependencies. Built to make finding the right tool feel calm, not exhausting.
bohioSubtitle: Bridge Our Humanities with Input & Output
bohioDesc: A pane beside your terminal — a local AI apprentice, civic-minded, intentionally silent until called. Not a productivity hack. A literacy tool.
bohioTriggerNote: ↑ triggers Sidecar, not executed in shell
privacyItem1: Powered by axem-sx/boh-io via local Ollama — no cloud, no external calls.
privacyItem2: Command history exists only in RAM for the duration of the open window.
privacyItem3: When you close Boh-IO, the entire conversation is wiped. No disk logs.
privacyItem4: The AI NEVER types into your shell — pane separation is absolute.
bohioConstraints: Note: Boh-IO does not support full-screen TUI applications (vim, htop, tmux) — they require cursor movements Boh-IO intentionally blocks to keep history linear. Use Konsole for those.
bohioMoreInDocs: First-time setup steps live in the Release Notes (zypper install · ollama pull · launch).
archSub: What AXEM-SX inherits, what it changes, and why.
